items.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: when I went into Lunceford’s band, well out of Chick Carter’s band, when I went in there, I replaced the lead trumpet player in Lunceford’s band.

ctx.x: What was the first group that you got to play lead with?

Well I was playing lead with this band that I mentioned, Chick Carter’s band. And I learned how to play lead in that band. ‘Cause I really didn’t want to be — I had no idea I was going to be a lead trumpet player. ‘Cause I wanted to be Louis Armstrong or Roy Eldridge or one of those kind of cats. And but when I went into Lunceford’s band, well out of Chick Carter’s band, when I went in there, I replaced the lead trumpet player in Lunceford’s band. His name was —

items.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I went in Jimmie Lunceford‘s band and replaced the first trumpet player, Eddie Tompkins.

ctx.x: Sy Oliver, there you go. He replaced Sy Oliver, but Sy Oliver wasn‘t no lead trumpet player either, but he did a lot of arrangements. The lead trumpet player, Gerald replaced Sy Oliver, I went in Jimmie Lunceford‘s band and replaced the first trumpet player, Eddie Tompkins.
Right. Ok, so how come you replaced him? Why did Eddie Tompkins leave the band?
